newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds consolidate resistance break.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds consolidate resistance break.

text.p: *Australian bonds close firmer after an opening flurry sees them break through resistance. Some selling sees them off their highs, consolidating their morning gains.
*News of small rise in December imports has no impact.
Australian bonds ended stronger after an early flurry of futures-led buying took bonds through resistance, triggering stop-loss orders and seeing spreads to Treasuries narrow markedly.

After a flattish close in the U.S. on Friday, with the U.S. Treasury market closed in both Tokyo and New York for a holiday, no local leads for the market and ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan appearing before a Senate committee on Tuesday, the early strength caught traders off-guard.
"It was really just 10-year futures initially, everything else lagged well behind that," one trader said.
"The volumes seemed to pickup as the market went a little bit higher suggesting there were stop loss levels being reached," the trader said.
At the highs, traders said some domestic sellers appeared, but bonds held firm above their previous resistance levels.
News of a 0.8 percent rise in merchandise imports in December, although stronger than expected, had no noticeable impact on the market.
Greenspan's committee appearance is the next key event for bonds, with traders saying it will determine market sentiment on the U.S. rate outlook ahead of February's FOMC meeting.

Spreads narrow markedly as local bonds outperform with the long end leading. Spreads to American bonds narrow to levels last seen around the beginning of 1994, and the potential for outperformance should remain in the leadup to December quarter CPI next week.
